sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system combining Roman-Dutch civil law tradition with English common-law principles, constitutional supremacy, and customary international law; unitary national company law under the Companies Act, 2008
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: South Africa-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement
South Africa-United States Double Taxation Agreement
Agreement Establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act, 2008 (Act No. 71 of 2008), sections 56 and 57 read with Companies Regulations, 2011 (Regulations 10A, 32 and 33); General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act, 2022 (Act No. 22 of 2022); Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (Act No. 38 of 2001), as amended; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorist and Related Activities Act, 2004 (Act No. 33 of 2004); CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register prescribed forms CoR 39A and CoR 39B

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each natural-person shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority in the country of domicile, followed by a South African notary public or authorised commissioner of oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the country-of-origin competent authority if the origin is an Apostille Convention state; otherwise South African consular legalization at the South African diplomatic mission of that country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential and business address of each director and beneficial owner (e.g., utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility services provider or regulated financial institution in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification by a South African notary public; foreign-origin documents require an apostille in an Apostille Convention state or consular legalization in non-apostille states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the South African incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the notary's competent authority, or consular legalization by the South African embassy if the origin state is not an Apostille party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent to act as first director in the prescribed CIPC form
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each initial director of the proposed (Pty) Ltd
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial certification within South Africa; no apostille required if executed in South Africa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of constitutional documents and board resolution of any corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or registered secretary of the foreign corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the corporate owner's jurisdiction if an Apostille Convention state; otherwise consular legalization by South African diplomatic mission

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders and UBOs must be screened against the South African domestic terrorism/terrorist financing list under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorist and Related Activities Act, updated UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, and European Union restrictive measures. FIC Guidance Note 5 requires enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) and stipulates identity verification, source of funds, and source of wealth documentation. The digital store publishing sector is categorised as Low_Risk_Standard under a risk-based approach, but beneficial ownership records must be filed with CIPC before or within the statutory post-incorporation filing window.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC Online Transacting System (e-services at www.cipc.co.za), administered by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name may be registered in any of South Africa's 12 official languages; however, CIPC records use Latin-alphabet transliteration. If the proposed name is in a language other than English or Afrikaans, the incorporating agent should provide a concise English translation or explanation of the meaning. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing company name, registered trademark, or protected commercial mark, and must not contain prohibited connotations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon CIPC name rejection, the applicant is formally notified with a reason code. The incorporating agent may immediately re-file a revised name application. If the applicant disputes the CIPC finding, a formal written representation may be submitted to the Companies Tribunal under section 154(2) of the Companies Act, 2008 and Regulation 98 of the Companies Regulations, 2011, within 30 business days of the rejection notice. A company name reservation that is refused may also be challenged by way of an administrative review application to the High Court if the CIPC decision is unlawful or procedurally unfair.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only as a managed service address if the service provider maintains a physical South African street address where service of legal process can be executed, where notices may be delivered, and where the company's statutory records are made available for inspection. A PO Box or purely virtual address without a physical reception and record-keeping capability does not satisfy section 23(1)-(3) of the Companies Act, 2008.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annual likelihood of unannounced physical inspection in the standard non-licensed PC and console digital publishing sector; CIPC may verify registered office compliance and address liveness, while the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) has enhanced on-site inspection powers if AML trigger indicators arise.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC name reservation fee (Form CoR 9) including name search and comparable name check
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prescribed statutory tariff under the Companies Regulations, 2011

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC incorporation filing fee (Notice of Incorporation and primary registration of the (Pty) Ltd)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prescribed statutory fee for standard company registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the Memorandum of Incorporation and ancillary resolutions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard MOI drafting based on hourly fee structures

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial certification of directors' and UBOs' passports, consents, and power of attorney bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial professional tariffs commonly charged per document; assumed five documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostille or consular legalization of foreign-origin UBO and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the foreign country of origin or South African consular mission
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Foreign apostille consular fee schedules; South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) authentication fees as applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service address for the first annual term (physical street address and statutory records facility)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate service provider or registered office vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for registered office maintenance and process-service reception

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN sanctions and South African terrorism list screening of directors, shareholders, and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-screening module market benchmark for low-risk standard commercial entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register first filing with CIPC after incorporation (CoR 39A / 39B submission and regulatory confirmation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee plus agent facilitation tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; applicable sections include 1 (definitions), 4 (solvency and liquidity), 13 (incorporation), 14 (registration and certificate), 19 (legal personality), 23 (name), 66-78 (board and directors); Companies Regulations 2011 (CoR forms and procedures)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), established under section 185 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; filings submitted through the CIPC e-Services portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI); registration is evidenced by the Certificate of Incorporation issued under section 14
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; authorised share capital is prescribed in the MOI and shares may be issued for nominal consideration subject to the solvency and liquidity test under section 4; no escrow account is required by CIPC for a (Pty) Ltd
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The incorporation of the Company under section 13 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 be ratified; the directors are authorised to finalise all CIPC and SARS filings. 2. The subscription for shares set out in the register of members be approved, and subscriber funds be credited to share capital. 3. The registered office be established at [Street, City, Province], South Africa, and filed with CIPC. 4. [Name] be appointed as CEO and [Name] as Financial Director, with authority to open bank accounts and execute contracts within approved limits. Approved by the board of directors on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services name reservation module (www.cipc.co.za) or a registered incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the CIPC database; file Form CoR 9.1 (reservation of name) listing up to four preferred names in order of priority; pay the ZAR 50 reservation fee; the reserved name is held for six months for incorporation; select a distinctive name that is not identical or deceptively similar to existing registered company names and is not offensive or contrary to public policy.
required_dossiers: CoR 9.1 Application for Reservation of Name
Copy of South African ID or foreign passport of applicant
Notarised power of attorney (if filed by an agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, lodge a fresh CoR 9.1 with alternative names or submit written representations to the CIPC Name Committee/Tribunal; an existing reservation may be extended by formal application before its expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation and director consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating legal practitioner / company secretary / proposed directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the MOI in accordance with Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; elect substitutional provisions (share transfer restrictions, director quorum, audit exemption); define authorised share capital and initial directors; obtain each director's signed consent to act and appoint the first auditor or reviewing officer if required by the public interest score or the MOI.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Incorporation
Consent to act as director (CIPC standard form)
Consent to act as auditor/reviewing officer (if appointed)
Registered office address and proof of premises address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries provisions of the MOI, correct the cited section references and resubmit the amended MOI with the same incorporation application; unresolved queries may require refiling a fresh CoR 14.1 with the revised MOI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of Notice of Incorporation and issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CoR 14.1, attach the signed MOI and consents, pay the ZAR 175 registration fee (approximately USD 10), and submit electronically; CIPC screens the file and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which evidences that the company holds legal personality from the date of issue.
required_dossiers: Signed CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation
CoR 9.1 name reservation certificate
Director consents and registered office details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any CIPC query notice within the stated period in the e-Services workspace, correct the documentation, and resubmit; if the application is repeatedly rejected, appeal to the Companies Tribunal or file a new application with rectified MOI and forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with SARS immediately after incorporation: obtain a Corporate Income Tax reference number; register for VAT if taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 annually; register for PAYE/UIF once employees are appointed; appoint a Public Officer within one month of commencement of business and link the SARS profile to the company bank account for refunds.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
SARS eFiling registration forms (CIT/VAT/PAYE)
Public Officer appointment confirmation
Director IDs and proof of business address
Bank confirmation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS registration is delayed, book a SARS branch appointment via eFiling, file the interim registration manually at a SARS branch, and obtain a Tax Compliance Status document to evidence the active registration during processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial ownership and statutory records filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services beneficial ownership module and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Compile a Beneficial Ownership Register identifying every natural person who directly or indirectly holds or controls economic or voting rights (above the indicative 5% threshold) or exercises effective control; file the register with CIPC on Form CoR 14.3 within 10 business days of incorporation; thereafter file the register annually with the annual return (CoR 14.4); file CoR 15.2 if the registered office changes; maintain minute and share registers at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Beneficial Ownership Register (per Companies Regulations 2011)
CoR 14.3 Beneficial Ownership filing
CoR 14.4 annual return annexure (annual update)
Shareholders list and shareholding percentages
CoR 15.2 Notice of Change of Registered Office (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC returns the beneficial ownership filing for inconsistency, reconcile the shareholding and control data, resubmit with a board affidavit explaining any divergences, and settle any administrative penalty before further non-compliance assessments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance book, banking and Steam/console payout onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors, appointed commercial bank, and payout platforms (Valve/PlayStation) as payment creditors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, issue share certificates, open the corporate bank account under FICA-compliant identity verification, and assemble the due diligence pack for Steam (Valve) and PlayStation Store payout onboarding: company extract, SARS compliance status, bank confirmation, and signed publishing agreements in the company's legal name.
required_dossiers: Minutes and signed first board resolution
Share certificates and share register
CIPC Certificate of Incorporation and company extract
SARS tax registration and compliance status document
FICA-compliant director identity and address proofs
Bank account confirmation letter in company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or payout platform rejects the dossier, obtain a consolidated CIPC company extract, an updated SARS tax clearance certificate, and a bank-verified account letter and resubmit the corrected pack to the relevant onboarding team.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (occupational health and safety) and the relevant local municipality (zoning and business premises) - no sectoral industrial licence is applicable to ISIC 5820 digital software publishing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for the publishing activity; a Film and Publication Board (FPB) classification may be triggered only if locally distributing physical media, whereas Steam and PlayStation Store platforms apply their own age-rating gatekeeping; municipal trading licence under the Business Act 71 of 1991 applies only to restricted trades, which does not include software publishing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) under the National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998 (NEMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based software publishing does not trigger Listing Notices 1-3 environmental authorisation activities; registration under the NEM: Waste Act 59 of 2008 may apply only if waste generation thresholds are exceeded
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated; office e-waste (IT equipment) must be handed to registered recyclers per Waste Act regulations; uninterruptible power supply batteries must be stored and disposed in accordance with SANS hazardous waste rules; any standby generator requires atmospheric emission licensing only above 10 MW capacity, which is not applicable to standard office operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the municipal fire authority for the office; occupational health and safety clearance under the OHSA 85 of 1993 including first aid equipment, fire extinguishers, electrical installation certificate (SANS 10142) and a written workplace risk assessment; no structural load certification is required for standard office floor loading

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at www.sarsefiling.co.za; head office at 299 Bronkhorst Street, Brooklyn, Pretoria. SARS is the sole national tax authority; no provincial/state-level tax registration exists in South Africa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate (Pty) Ltd with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) to obtain the enterprise registration number. 2) Register the company as a taxpayer via SARS eFiling to secure an income tax reference number; appoint a Public Officer (s24 Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011) within one month of incorporation. 3) Apply for VAT registration through Form VAT 101 where taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory, s23(1) VAT Act 89 of 1991) or ZAR 50,000 (voluntary, s23(3)); foreign-owned local subsidiaries follow the same process and require a local director and SARS-mandated banking details in South Africa. 4) Register for Customs Code if physical import/export of goods occurs (not required for pure digital Steam/PlayStation publishing).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — tax-resident South African company taxed at 27% corporate income tax on worldwide income under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; no pass-through to shareholders; distributions subject to 20% dividends tax (s64D) unless a shareholder exemption applies; branch profits of foreign operations are subject to CFC attribution rules (s9D); no territorial election is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in South African law. Available elections relevant to digital publishing: (i) VAT group registration election under s50 VAT Act for groups of connected persons with ≥50% holding; (ii) s45 intra-group corporate restructure roll-over election; (iii) s23M hybrid mismatch deneturalization/adjustment elections for cross-border instruments; (iv) s9D CFC foreign business establishment exclusion election and high-taxed CFC election; (v) s24I forex realization elections where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) — Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS; no separate GST or sales and use tax applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,000,000 of taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months or reasonably expected in the next 12 months (s23(1) VAT Act). Voluntary registration: ZAR 50,000 (s23(3)). Once registered, VAT 201 returns are filed on a monthly or bi-monthly basis; standard 15% rate, 0% zero-rated exports, and exempt supplies under s12 of the VAT Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping regime is currently in force. SARS eFiling is the mandatory electronic channel for VAT 201 returns and tax invoices must comply with s20 VAT Act (full tax invoice for supplies exceeding ZAR 5,000; abridged for ZAR 5,000 or less; recipient-created tax invoices require prior SARS approval). SARS published an OECD-aligned e-invoicing policy framework in 2023 with phased voluntary adoption through certified PEPPOL/SDI service providers; mandatory clearance is not yet legislated. For digital platform payouts (Steam/PlayStation), the taxpayer must retain platform settlement reports and reconcile them to VAT return outputs.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under s11(1)(a) of the VAT Act for goods physically exported, and under s11(2)(b) for services supplied to a non-resident who is not in South Africa at the time of supply, provided the services are not directly in connection with land or movable property in South Africa and are not consumed or used in South Africa. For PC/console game publishing via Steam/PlayStation: (i) license/supply of digital game rights to Valve Corporation (Steam, non-resident) or Sony Interactive Entertainment (non-resident) qualifies as an exported service at 0% where the recipient is outside South Africa and the platform-sourced revenue is earned outside South Africa; (ii) direct digital sales to South African end-users are subject to 15% VAT; (iii) the vendor must retain documentary proof of the non-resident recipient before applying zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) — required only where physical goods are exported; not applicable to pure digital downloads
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill — required only for physical goods; not applicable to digital Steam/PlayStation publishing
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT foreign-currency credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Signed license/distribution agreement with Steam (Valve Corp) or PlayStation Store (Sony) evidencing non-resident recipient and place of supply
Platform settlement reports (monthly payout statements) reconciling gross sales, platform fees, and net remittance in USD/EUR
Non-resident certificate or jurisdiction-of-establishment evidence for the platform counterparty
VAT export register (s11(2)) with invoice numbers, dates, currency, exchange rates, and proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS and the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 require export proceeds to be declared and repatriated to South Africa within 180 days of export/supply; failure triggers exchange-control penalties and administrative enforcement. Incorrect zero-rating claims are clawed back: VAT at 15% becomes payable with interest (s187 TAA); additional tax of up to 200% of the unpaid VAT may be imposed under s60(1) of the VAT Act; understatement penalties under Schedule 1 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 range from 10% (substantial non-compliance) to 200% (intentional tax evasion). Deliberate fraudulent zero-rating constitutes a criminal offense under s234–s235 TAA and the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964, carrying fines, imprisonment, and retrospective disgorgement; the burden of proof to substantiate zero-rating rests on the vendor (s102 TAA).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) – Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933) and the Exchange Control Regulations promulgated thereunder.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a dual-tier exchange control regime. Non-resident rand accounts and inward capital transfers are freely convertible for current account transactions, while capital account transactions by residents require specific FinSurv approval. Profit remittance for foreign investors is permissible after satisfying tax clearance and exchange control documentation: the payment must be made via an authorised dealer using an inward transfer reference and the beneficiary must be the non-resident shareholder. Resident companies may freely convert ZAR for genuine current trade, but outbound investment and asset transfers require FinSurv approval. The rand is a controlled currency; technological gaming revenue from Steam/PlayStation is classified as exported services and qualifies for full conversion upon surrender, but capacity to retain foreign currency earnings is capped.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All exports of goods or services (including digital gaming licences and royalties) must have proceeds received in the Republic through an authorised dealer within 30 days of the earlier of shipment or date of invoice, and the full foreign currency amount must be offered for immediate sale (surrendered) to the authorised dealer. Under the Exporters' Retention Protocol, a South African resident company may retain up to 5% of eligible foreign currency earnings in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) for operational needs, provided the remaining 95% is converted to ZAR in the interbank spot market; retention above 5% requires prior FinSurv approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
FirstRand Bank Limited (First National Bank Corporate and Investment Banking)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low – offshore digital EMIs (electronic money institutions) are not authorised dealers under the South African Exchange Control Regulations. South African resident entities are required to route all foreign exchange receipts and payments through authorised dealing banks. While EMI accounts may receive funds without formal approval if they operate outside the SARB authorisation perimeter, export surrender obligations and the inability of EMIs to supply transfer evidence can trigger exchange control penalties. Offshore EMI usage is viable only for incidental low-value collections subject to prompt repatriation through an authorised dealer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director (or designated senior officer) and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) is mandated at an appointed branch or via SARB-approved electronic FICA remote verification (video KYC). A fully digital, never-met onboarding is not accepted by the big four banks; each director signing on the account must complete FICA due diligence, with beneficial ownership registration and source-of-funds declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent business profile – a software publishing company receiving recurring cross-border gaming payouts from Valve Corp (Steam) and Sony Interactive Entertainment (PlayStation Store) without local operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the licensed distribution agreement (publishing contract), commercial invoices to Steam Parent and Sony, Steamworks/PlayStation Partner registration, payroll/office lease records, and historical bank statements showing the matching payouts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity – shareholding through a foreign holding company without a clear UBO chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) beneficial ownership record, shareholder register, sworn declarations, Memorandum of Incorporation, and a diagram of the ownership chain up to individual natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FX surrender non-compliance red flag – retained foreign currency proceeds on FCA beyond the 5% retention limit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent FCA transaction statements, an internally prepared FX retention calculation, SARB/authorised dealer approval letters for exemption, and a documented conversion schedule showing the mandatory 95% surrender within 30 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for capital injection unclear – large inward transfer from a related offshore entity for share capital subscription.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A completed SARB Form A (inward transfer information), board resolution authorising share issuance, share subscription agreement, source-of-funds bank statements from the sending entity, and tax clearance of the recipient company.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign equity capital must be remitted in the investor's name via SWIFT (MT103/MT202) to the company's authorised dealer bank using the SARB purpose code 'Foreign Direct Investment – Equity Capital'. The company submits SARB Form A and a Beneficiary Identification and Source of Funds declaration. Funds are credited to the company's FCA or converted to ZAR at the impact of the authorised dealer. Subsequent share allotment must be filed with CIPC and supported by a share register. For shareholder loans, Form C along with loan agreement, interest terms, and FinSurv approval must be obtained.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Current-account outbound payments for software royalties, platform fees, and developer profit share must be cleared via SWIFT MT103 through an authorised dealer, accompanied by a tax clearance certificate (s 33 of the Income Tax Act), invoice, LR (Exchange Control) declaration, and proof of services rendered. Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) are used only for physical merchandise trade; digital payouts to Steam/PlayStation platforms are executed via MT103/MT202 instructions under the SARB's 'Computer and information services' BOP code, with no requirement for an LC. Payment timers must respect the 7-day (domestic) and 30-day (cross-border) regulatory settlement cycles.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contracts (FECs) for hedging forecast ZAR cash flow of foreign currency receivables
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) permitted with an authorised dealer or offshore for non-resident hedges, where the underlying cannot be delivered, subject to SARB policy
Cross-currency swaps to match future foreign currency working capital obligations
FX swap transactions for short-term liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return of the Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of the company's incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties apply from the 31st business day after the anniversary; continued failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off or deregistration under Section 82(3)(b) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted together with the annual return; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 business days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an offence under the Companies Act; directors and officers are liable to a fine of up to ZAR 500,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 10 years; the company may also be flagged as non-compliant in the CIPC records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the financial year-end, or such other date prescribed by SARS for provisional taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Understatement Penalty of 10%–30% depending on the conduct category; interest charged monthly on unpaid tax; SARS may issue a notice of non-compliance and institute civil collection proceedings for persistent non-filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory if the Public Interest Score (PIS) equals or exceeds 350; if the PIS is between 100 and 349, the company must obtain an independent review unless it is a public, state-owned, or regulated company; private companies with a PIS below 100 are exempt from audit unless required by the Memorandum of Incorporation or shareholder consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for companies with public accountability; IFRS for SMEs or full IFRS for private companies; no separate South African local GAAP is prescribed.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Register of Beneficial Ownership and confirm the correctness of beneficial ownership data through the CIPC annual return process. The annual return must disclose any shareholding transfers during the year and identify all natural persons with beneficial ownership. Any transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed with CIPC within 30 business days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing minutes of member and director meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $200–$600 per annum for registered office service and company secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,500–$8,000 per annum for a certified audit or independent review of a small private software publishing company

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to a standard (Pty) Ltd. Preferential provisions include: Section 11D research and development tax deduction (150% qualifying R&D expenditure for video-game/software development, subject to SARS certification), Section 12B accelerated capital allowance for renewable energy assets, Section 12H learnership allowance, Employment Tax Incentive (ETI) for qualifying employees, and a reduced 15% corporate rate for qualifying Special Economic Zone entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_rule: Assessed losses are carried forward indefinitely; for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023, the loss set-off is limited to the lower of the remaining assessed loss and 80% of taxable income computed before the set-off.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) filed through the SARS eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za); provisional taxpayers also submit IRP6 returns via eFiling.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax payments are made bi-annually with an optional top-up.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year (year of assessment). First provisional payment is due within six months of the beginning of the year; second provisional payment is due no later than the last day of the year; and the top-up payment is due within six months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, trade name, entity ID, financial year-end date, and registered office details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident (Pty) Ltd must indicate its place of effective management and SARS branch registration for a South African permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirms whether the company is South African resident (incorporated in SA or effectively managed in SA).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If resident by incorporation but managed abroad, an international ruling or supporting board minutes should be attached to prove non-residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross receipts from Steam/PlayStation Store digital publishing, including VAT-exclusive sales and royalty streaming revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only South Africa-source income and must attach a source analysis and payer statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable receipts, arm's-length expenditure, allowances, and Section 11D R&D expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are limited to expenses attributable to South African PE activity; no head-office or offshore IP expense can be netted without transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of prior-year assessed loss brought forward and current-year loss, applying the 80% set-off limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses attributable to a SA PE may be carried forward only against profits of that PE while the company remains non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of connected-party transactions, cross-border IP licences, management charges, and loans.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlling shareholders must attach the TP policy and confirm arm's-length parameters; SARS can adjust if documentation is absent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed normal tax, reduced by provisional tax payments (IRP6 credits), foreign tax credits, and tax rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident with a PE must reconcile SA-source taxes and claim DTA foreign tax credits where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers administrative non-compliance penalties under TAA ss 210-211: monthly penalty of at least ZAR 250, rising to 10% of assessed tax per month for high-income companies; understatement penalties under TAA s 222 up to 200%; late-payment interest and a 10% late-payment penalty; and criminal exposure (fine up to ZAR 10 million and/or imprisonment up to five years).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% Dividend Tax (Section 64EA of the Income Tax Act) on all dividends paid by the South African company, subject to exemptions for certain South African resident shareholders and treaty reductions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit the SARS Declaration for Reduced Dividend Tax (Form DTR01) to the withholding agent before the dividend payment, accompanied by a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign jurisdiction and evidence of beneficial ownership. The withholding agent applies the treaty rate (commonly 0%, 5% or 10%) instead of the statutory 20%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory final withholding tax; most DTAs reduce the rate to 0–10% for beneficial owners. Interest: 15% statutory final withholding tax; treaty rates commonly 0–10% depending on the DTA, with a domestic-law exemption for listed bonds.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where the aggregate value of all affected transactions (cross-border connected-person transactions) exceeds ZAR 100 million in the year. Master File is required for a South African entity that is part of an MNE group with consolidated group revenue of at least ZAR 10 billion; Country-by-Country Reporting applies at the same ZAR 10 billion group-revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but substance is legally enforced through the place of effective management test, CFC provisions (s 9D), transfer pricing connected-person rules, and the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (s 80A-L). A company without employees, premises, or commercial function in South Africa will be disregarded or re-characterised for tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Steam/PlayStation payouts from gross income, fabricating deductions, destroying records, filing false ITR14 declarations, or using undeclared bank accounts to divert sale proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under TAA s 234: fine of up to ZAR 10 million and/or imprisonment up to five years. SARS concurrently imposes an understatement penalty under TAA s 222 up to 200% of the tax shortfall, plus interest and the 10% late-payment penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: SARS may hold a director personally and jointly liable for the company's unpaid tax where the director knowingly participated in the evasion; the director faces a travel ban, civil restitution orders, disqualification from management, and imprisonment upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Impermissible Tax Avoidance Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a (Pty) Ltd with no personnel, office, business activity, or economic risk, solely to hold gaming licences and revenue, invoice Steam/PlayStation, and distribute funds to a tax-indifferent foreign parent; or implementing circular financing to manufacture deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS applies GAAR (s 80A-L) to disregard the shell, re-characterise income, and deny all tax benefits; understatement penalty of 100%–200% of the assessed shortfall and criminal referral under TAA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly liable as parties to an impermissible avoidance arrangement and may be sued for restitution; asset-preservation orders and travel bans are common; criminal proceedings may lead to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Cross-Border Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties or licence fees to the foreign IP-owner parent, or underpricing distribution services, in respect of Steam/PlayStation publishing while failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS adjusts the consideration to arm's length under s 31 of the Income Tax Act, imposes consequential withholding tax on adjusted amounts where appropriate, and applies understatement penalties of up to 200% for deliberate or negligent failures; failure to keep records is a separate offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or implement the mispricing may become jointly subject to the assessed liability, civil restitution, travel bans, and, on criminal conviction, imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using opaque corporate vehicles or foreign shell accounts to receive Steam/PlayStation revenues, laundering proceeds through cryptocurrency or bearer instruments, failing to conduct beneficial-owner due diligence, and not filing suspicious-transaction reports where the company acts as a financial or gaming-service intermediary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FICA s 51C administrative fine up to ZAR 10 million per contravention (plus continuing daily penalties); POCA s 4 conviction: fine up to ZAR 100 million and/or imprisonment up to 30 years; asset forfeiture available under POCA Chapter 6.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly assist in money laundering face arrest, travel bans, asset freezes, personal civil forfeiture, imprisonment, and disqualification from the board.
